name: AndyClaw
vibe_summary: A full OpenClaw-style agentic assistant rebuilt as a native Android APK, with deep ethOS/dGEN1 integration including wallet control, XMTP messaging, and on-device reflex models. It stands out for its unusually rigorous security hardening (taint tracking, approval gating, staged skill installs) rare among mobile AI agents.
best_for: dGEN1/ethOS owners wanting deep OS-level AI control
Android users wanting a local-first agent with wallet integration
Crypto-native users who want an autonomous on-chain assistant
avoid_if: You need iOS or desktop support
You are uncomfortable granting an AI shell and device-control permissions
You want a large, battle-tested community ecosystem
openclaw_advantages: Native Android APK with full device control (calls, SMS, WiFi, apps)
On-device reflex models route requests in ~15 ms without a model call
Built-in crypto wallet and XMTP messaging on ethOS
Local Qwen2.5-1.5B option works with no API key
Strong taint-tracking and approval-gate security model
openclaw_disadvantages: Android-only; no desktop or multi-channel chat app support
Much smaller community and skill ecosystem
Best features locked to ethOS/dGEN1 hardware
Single-APK mobile form factor limits extensibility vs OpenClaw's stack
confidence_summary: README and commit history give strong evidence of architecture and security posture, but Reddit matches are unrelated noise and web sentiment is about OpenClaw generally, so community reception is highly uncertain.

overview_markdown:
AndyClaw is a native Android reimagining of the OpenClaw personal AI agent, shipped as a single APK by Freedom Factory. It runs an agentic tool-use loop (up to 20 tool iterations per turn) with two operating modes: a privileged mode on ethOS/dGEN1 devices that unlocks wallet transactions across multiple EVM chains, XMTP messaging, full device control, and an autonomous AI-controlled sub-account wallet; and an open mode on stock Android offering chat, SMS, contacts, shell commands, Termux integration, long-term memory, and ClawHub community skills.

Architecturally it is unusually ambitious for a mobile agent: it ships tiny on-device 'reflex' models (a 33M-parameter router and a fine-tuned Gemma 270M) that classify and resolve simple commands in milliseconds without any LLM call, falling back to a local Qwen2.5-1.5B or user-supplied OpenRouter/Tinfoil keys. A background heartbeat (OS-managed on ethOS, foreground service elsewhere) lets it act autonomously.

Where it most differs from OpenClaw is its security discipline: recent commits show taint tracking that blocks wallet actions after reading third-party content, staged and lockfile-pinned skill installs, SSRF-resistant web fetching, redaction of seed phrases from memory, and approval gating for sensitive tools. The trade-off is platform scope — it is Android-only, with its best features gated behind ethOS hardware, and a far smaller ecosystem than OpenClaw's multi-channel stack.
